definition.alternative: Preference divergence decays to zero once stochastic artifacts are fully controlled.
assumptions: Episodic retrieval biases subsequent action probabilities.
Controlled environments minimize exogenous stochastic noise.
Divergence slope remains non-negative across rigorous trials.
definition.falsification: Measured divergence slope drops significantly below zero, indicating convergence.
definition.statement: Memory-augmented agents exhibit stable non-zero policy divergence over extended training horizons in controlled environments when historical state trajectories are weighted by episodic retrieval, even under reduced variance conditions.
definition.uncertainty: Determining whether lower variance bounds completely eliminate residual drift.

definition.method: Execute a refined simulation measuring divergence slope over 80000 steps with tighter variance bounds.
definition.stop: Stop after 25 trials or if execution exceeds budget.
definition.success: Divergence slope remains non-negative with high confidence.
